subtitle: A kingdom restored in chains of velvet and steel

panels.shot: epic split composition, half showing stormed walls of Srirangapatna, half a tiny boy on a throne under looming British officers
panels.action: Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits stiff and wide-eyed on an ornate throne in Mysore, while in a shadowed half of the frame ruined battlements of Srirangapatna and distant British soldiers suggest the violent path to his crown.

dialogue.text: In 1799, as Tipu Sultan fell at Srirangapatna, a four-year-old Wodeyar was crowned in Mysore, rescued by British power yet bound by it for life.

i18n.hi: १७९९ में, श्रीरंगपट्टन में टीपू सुल्तान गिरते ही, चार साल के वोडेयार को मैसूर में ताज पहनाया गया — अंग्रेजी ताकत ने बचाया, पर उसी ने उम्र भर बाँध भी दिया।

panels.shot: wide overhead view of Srirangapatna fort at dawn, British lines encircling, smoke hanging low
panels.action: The island fortress of Srirangapatna crouches in the Kaveri’s embrace at dawn, British siege lines and batteries encircling its battered walls under a haze of smoke and dust.

dialogue.text: May 1799. Srirangapatna stands ringed by Company guns. For four months, Tipu Sultan has fought a power that comes with ledgers and bayonets.

i18n.hi: मई १७९९। कंपनी की तोपों ने श्रीरंगपट्टन को घेर रखा है। चार महीने से टीपू सुल्तान उस ताकत से भिड़ा है, जो बही–खाते और संगीनें साथ लाती है।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of British storming party rushing a breached wall under cannon smoke
panels.action: Red-coated British and sepoy soldiers surge through a gaping breach in the fort wall, faces set, bayonets glinting in the smoky, dust-thick light as Mysore defenders fall back in confusion.

dialogue.text: On 4 May, the breach is stormed. Beatson’s pen will later praise discipline and courage, but the smoke hides the fear on both sides.

i18n.hi: ४ मई को किला टूटा, झोंक कर हमला हुआ। बीटसन की कलम बाद में अनुशासन और बहादुरी गाएगी, धुआँ दोनों तरफ का डर छुपा लेगा।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot near the Water Gate, British officers with lanterns finding a fallen figure implied as Tipu
panels.action: In the twilight near the Water Gate passage, British officers bend with lanterns over a richly armoured form lying still amid shattered masonry, their faces grave in the flickering light.

dialogue.text: Near the Water Gate, Tipu lies dead, cut down in the chaos. Stories of betrayal will spread, but records show only confusion and a final, desperate defence.

i18n.hi: पानी दरवाज़े के पास टीपू गिरा पड़ा है, हड़बड़ी में कटा हुआ। गद्दारी की कहानियाँ फैलेंगी, पर काग़ज़ों में बस अफरातफरी और आख़िरी, बेताब लड़ाई है।

panels.shot: wide interior of Tipu's audience hall, British officers and allies standing over empty throne
panels.action: Inside Tipu’s grand audience hall, his lion-emblazoned throne stands empty as British officers consult maps and papers, while allied Indian rulers stand watchful at the edges of the polished floor.

dialogue.text: With Tipu gone, Mysore is leaderless. Wellesley’s dispatches speak of settlement, not plunder, but every line weighs revenue, routes and allies.

i18n.hi: टीपू के जाते ही मैसूर बिन सरदार का है। वेलज़्ली के परचे लूट नहीं, ‘समझौते’ की बात करते हैं, पर हर पंक्ति में ख़ज़ाना, रास्ते और रफ़ीक़ तौले जाते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate interior scene, low-angle of a toddler Krishnaraja in a modest Mysore residence, elders around him
panels.action: In a modest Mysore house, tiny Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits cross-legged, clutching a small wooden toy, as elders in simple white cotton whisper urgent words and glance towards the door.

dialogue.text: Far from the breached walls, a child plays. Krishnaraja Wodeyar, barely four, is scion of a line that once ruled this land before Haidar and Tipu.

i18n.hi: टूटी दीवारों से दूर एक बच्चा खेल रहा है। कृष्णराज वोडेयार, बस चार बरस का, उसी वंश का वारिस जिसने हैदर और टीपू से पहले ये धरती संभाली थी।

panels.shot: mid-shot of British officer gently addressing the child, elders watching anxiously
panels.action: A British officer in blue frock coat kneels slightly to address young Krishnaraja, whose eyes are wide and uncertain, while Wodeyar family elders stand tense and hopeful behind him.

dialogue.text: Company officers come with a proposal: restore the old dynasty under their protection. A boy will wear the crown; the Company will hold the sword.

i18n.hi: कंपनी अफ़सर एक तरकीब लेकर आते हैं: पुरानी राजवंशी बहाल, पर उनकी छतरी में। ताज सिर पर बालक का, तलवार हाथ में कंपनी की।

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot inside a Mysore palace hall, coronation in progress with British presence discreet but visible
panels.action: In a richly decorated hall, young Krishnaraja sits on a low golden throne, garlanded, as priests perform rituals; at the rear, British officers and officials stand observing, their uniforms a stark contrast to silk and sandalwood.

dialogue.text: In 1799, the capital moves back to Mysore. The child is crowned Maharaja, while a treaty of subsidiary alliance quietly fixes British suzerainty over his realm.

i18n.hi: १७९९ में राजधानी फिर मैसूर लौटती है। बच्चे को महाराजा बनाया जाता है, और साथ ही एक अधीन गठबंध का करार चुपचाप उसके राज्य पर अंग्रेज़ बादशाहत जड़ देता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder from behind a British official showing treaty document being presented near the throne
panels.action: Seen over the shoulder of a British official, a neatly penned treaty, seals dangling, is held out towards Wodeyar ministers standing by the small Maharaja, who looks on, not yet able to read the words that bind him.

dialogue.text: The treaty obliges Mysore to accept a resident, maintain a British force, pay subsidy, and cede territory. Sovereignty returns, but wrapped in clauses and conditions.

i18n.hi: करार मैसूर को रेसिडेंट मानने, अंग्रेज़ फौज रखने, गरदा देने और ज़मीन छोड़ने को बाँधता है। हुकूमत लौटती है, पर धाराओं और शर्तों में लिपटी हुई।

panels.shot: time-lapse style montage, young Krishnaraja growing, learning under tutors, British resident in background
panels.action: A layered image shows Krishnaraja as a boy with palm-leaf manuscripts, then as a youth with quill and paper, while in the background a British resident confers with Mysore officials under the same palace roof.

dialogue.text: Years pass. Krishnaraja grows into a learned prince, mastering music, literature, and statecraft, yet every major decision still needs the nod of the resident.

i18n.hi: साल बीतते हैं। कृष्णराज विद्वान राजकुमार बनता है — संगीत, साहित्य और राजकाज का उस्ताद — पर हर बड़ी बात पर आख़िरी सिर हिलाना रेसिडेंट का ही रहता है।

panels.shot: mid-shot of the adult maharaja on a balcony overlooking Mysore, papers in hand, worry on his face
panels.action: Now a young man, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III stands on a palace balcony overlooking Mysore’s bustling streets, holding revenue reports, his brow furrowed as monsoon clouds gather over the city.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii
dialogue.text: How to rule when each coin, each village, is weighed by others?

i18n.hi: कैसे राज करे, जब हर सिक्का, हर गाँव किसी और के तराज़ू में तौला जाए?

panels.shot: wide interior of durbar with British resident arguing with Mysore officials, maharaja seated uneasily
panels.action: In the durbar hall, Krishnaraja sits formally enthroned while the British resident and senior Mysore officials stand facing each other, hands raised in controlled argument over stacked ledgers and maps laid on a low table.

dialogue.text: By the 1820s, Company reports complain of misrule and deficit; the court speaks of drought, war burdens and interference. Two languages describe the same hardship.

i18n.hi: १८२० के दशक तक कंपनी की रिपोर्टें कुशासन और घाटे का रोना रोती हैं; दरबार सूखे, जंग के बोझ और दख़लअंदाज़ी का। दो ज़बानें, एक ही तकलीफ़ की दास्तान।

panels.shot: close-up of a British dispatch being sealed, Wellesley-era style, hands firm and practiced
panels.action: A British administrator’s hands fold a dispatch, the words about Mysore’s administration barely visible, then press hot wax and seal it with the Company’s emblem, the gesture brisk and final.

dialogue.text: In London and Calcutta, such reports feed a familiar conclusion: when a princely state falters, the Company must take the reins 'for the people’s good'.

i18n.hi: लंदन और कलकत्ता में ये काग़ज़ वही नतीजा खिलाते हैं: जब कोई रियासत लड़खड़ाए, तो ‘रियाया की भलाई’ के नाम पर कंपनी को लगाम अपने हाथ लेनी चाहिए।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of 1831 ceremony, British taking charge, maharaja in background, authority slipping
panels.action: In 1831, under grey skies, British officials formally receive symbolic emblems of authority from Mysore’s ministers, while Krishnaraja Wodeyar III stands in the background, composed but distant, hands clasped tightly.

dialogue.text: That year, the British declare direct administration. The Mysore Commission is born. The Maharaja keeps his title, but his hands are gently removed from the levers of power.

i18n.hi: उसी साल अंग्रेज़ सीधी हुकूमत का एलान करते हैं। ‘मैसूर कमीशन’ जन्म लेता है। महाराजा का ख़िताब बचता है, पर ताक़त के हत्थों से उसके हाथ नर्म–नर्म हटाए जाते हैं।

panels.shot: interior shot of the maharaja now in a more private setting, focusing on arts, manuscripts, and ritual
panels.action: In an inner hall lit by oil lamps, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III oversees a ritual, musicians gathered nearby, manuscripts and miniatures spread before him as he listens, his face calm yet shadowed by thought.

dialogue.text: Krishnaraja turns inward. If he cannot direct the treasury, he can shape culture, patronising music, painting, and a courtly life that keeps Wodeyar identity alive under Commission rule.

i18n.hi: कृष्णराज भीतर की ओर मुड़ता है। ख़ज़ाना नहीं चला सकता तो रंग–रस चला सकता है — संगीत, चित्रकला और दरबारी असबाब को सहारा देकर, कमीशन राज में भी वोडेयार की छाप जिंदा रखता है।

panels.shot: contrasting split scene, one side British-built public work, other side palace ritual continuing
panels.action: A split composition shows, on one side, a British officer supervising a new road and canal with Indian labourers, and on the other, a palace courtyard where traditional rituals and processions continue under the gaze of courtiers.

dialogue.text: Under the Commission, roads, tanks and offices spread across Mysore. Yet the palace remains a second centre, a reminder that this order is not purely colonial nor purely royal.

i18n.hi: कमीशन के नीचे सड़कों, टैंकों और दफ़्तरों का जाल मैसूर भर में फैलता है। पर महल दूसरी अड्डी बना रहता है, याद दिलाता है कि ये निज़ाम न पूरा फिरंगी है न पूरा शाही।

panels.shot: forward-looking wide shot suggesting later 1881 restoration, a child Wodeyar glimpsed alongside British and Indian elites
panels.action: In a forward-leaning image, a later child of the Wodeyar line stands in ceremonial dress beside British and Indian elites, a faint suggestion of a new coronation hall behind them, hinting at a restoration yet to come.

dialogue.text: In 1881, long after Krishnaraja’s youth, powers return again to his house. Mysore becomes a 'model' princely state, its modernity born from both constraint and adaptation.

i18n.hi: १८८१ में, कृष्णराज की जवानी बहुत पीछे छूट चुकी, ताक़त फिर उसके घर लौटती है। मैसूर ‘नमूना’ रियासत कहलाता है — जहाँ नौकरशाही और नवाबी, दोनों से मिलकर नया ज़माना पैदा होता है।

panels.shot: quiet close-up on an older Krishnaraja's face in profile, half-lit, palace lattice casting patterned shadow
panels.action: An older Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits by a carved lattice window, his profile half-lit, patterned shadows falling across his thoughtful eyes as he gazes out over a city that has changed around him.

dialogue.text: His life began as a restoration and passed into restraint. In him we see how power can be returned in form yet redirected in substance, and how a kingdom can survive by bending without fully breaking.

i18n.hi: उसकी ज़िंदगी बहाली से शुरू हुई, फिर बंधनों में ढल गई। उसमें हम देख सकते हैं, कैसे हुक्म की शक्ल लौटा दी जाए, पर मजमून बदला जाए; और कैसे एक रियासत टूटे बगैर झुक कर भी जी सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: A kingdom restored in chains of velvet and steel
subtitle_i18n.hi: रेशम और इस्पात की जंजीरों में लौटा हुआ राज्य
